newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds were trading higher into the close on Tuesday tracking foreign markets, but just off session highs after a spell of profit taking during the afternoon.
"We saw mostly domestic buying today," a dealer in Madrid said. He added the trading volume had not been that high and the Spanish market was following the euphoria of others.

Long term bond futures set a record high at 111.77 but by 1610 GMT they were trading at 111.40, up 14 basis points. The 10-year spread over German bunds widened slightly before the close to 131 bps, after trading around 126 bps earlier.
"On the cash market we aim to go below resistance at the seven percent level on the 10-year yield," said one dealer.
The three year 7.80 percent bond closed at 104.45 from 104.31 at Monday's close, with a yield of 6.049 percent.
"The yield curve is flattening in anticipation of a fresh rate cut before year end," one dealer said.
At Wednesday's public auction of one-year T-bills dealers expect a high level of bids with yields seen declining to a record low of around six percent.
